t: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the United States courthouse and Federal building referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Edward J. Devitt United States Courthouse and Federal Building”.

fable.w: This is a naming provision that tells readers how to interpret references to a federal building in existing records. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" signals rulemaking, but here it only appears in a list of documents where the building's name may occur; no rulemaking is authorized or required. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given any role in a federal decision.
fable.s: shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Edward J. Devitt United States Courthouse and Federal Building”

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely administrative renaming provision. It dictates how a specific federal building should be referred to in official records. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. There is no advisory board, public hearing, or comment period mentioned.
qwen_block.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the United States courthouse and Federal building referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Edward J. Devitt United States Courthouse and Federal Building”.
